policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'that they might bring us into bondage' renders the purpose clause without marking future indicative active against aorist subjunctive middle; the lone note is alternative_rendering ('Or, but it was because of') and touches the opening clause, not this verb.
Presence or absence of the article before θεός is invisible in English; ASV 'God accepteth not man's person' is identical under either reading, and both notes are alternative_rendering.

ASV 'that we should go unto the Gentiles, and they unto the circumcision' leaves the correlative particle unrendered, as English regularly does with μέν; nothing in the wording shows whether it stood.
ASV names 'Cephas came to Antioch', rendering Κηφᾶς, not Πέτρος.
ASV 'before that certain came from James ... but when they came' takes a plural subject with a plural verb, rendering ἦλθον rather than singular ἦλθεν.
ASV renders the conjunction: 'And the rest of the Jews dissembled likewise with him', so καί stood; the omission would leave the clause asyndetic.
ASV 'I said unto Cephas before them all' renders Κηφᾷ, not Πέτρῳ.

The readings differ only in where ζῇς stands and whether the negative is spelled out; English must place the verb before both adverbs, so ASV 'livest as do the Gentiles, and not as do the Jews' comes out the same under every order.
οὐκ and οὐχί are orthographic variants of the same negative; ASV 'and not as do the Jews' cannot distinguish them.
ASV asks 'how compellest thou the Gentiles', rendering πῶς; τί would give 'why'.
ASV 'yet knowing that a man is not justified' renders an adversative connective, which the omission would leave nothing to translate.
ASV has 'through faith in Jesus Christ' at this point (contrasting with 'believed on Christ Jesus' later in the verse), rendering the order Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

ASV 'because by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified' puts the prepositional phrase before the verb, matching ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται rather than the RP order with the verb first.
συνιστάνω and συνίστημι are alternative present forms of one verb with the same sense; ASV 'I prove myself a transgressor' cannot distinguish them.
ASV 'the faith which is in the Son of God, who loved me' renders υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, not θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ.
